chapter: Auditions, musicians and the jazz club
title: Musicians and drinking
summary: They recall how much the musicians drank, Jim Robinson's bottle, and the sweating of playing.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: A lot of them drank. There may have been some that didn't, but most of them did.
Jim is the one I remember drinking some then. Jim. He's jolly, but not drinking to excess.
Yeah, but I don't remember him being unable to play.
No, nor do I. But I do remember him having a fifth on the bandstand in some places. Sitting there. Yes. Yeah. But it looked as though he was the one who was drinking from it pretty much exclusively.
Of course, Billy and the D drank. Yeah.
I remember that being more talk about drinking than I could drink. I'll put it that way. People would comment on how much people could drink. But they seemed to be able to hold it.
Yeah. I don't remember much saying anybody drunk. I know that whenever they take a break in a nightclub, they would show up with a drink. Yeah. Most of them.
Because we don't know what that drink was. That's true. Maybe it was Shirley Temple. Sure. That makes sense if you're thirsty to drink a lot. Sure.
Yeah. Hot and then just the physical blowing of a horn makes you thirsty. Sure. See.
I remember a lot of sweating.
